campaign_name: Protect Education, Accountability Now (ESA eligibility and spending limits initiative)
purpose: Limit Empowerment Scholarship Account eligibility to families earning under $150,000 (starting 2027-28) and bar luxury purchases and paying family members
sponsor: Protect Education, Accountability Now campaign (endorsed by Arizona Education Association and Save Our Schools Arizona)
evidence_note: Only one of six 2026 Arizona initiatives filed signatures. No firm named in the source. A 400K+ drive in Arizona almost always uses paid circulators, but no source here confirms it. Check the AZ SOS paid-circulator registry or SeeTheMoney to see who was paid.

campaign_name: Protect the Vote Arizona (constitutional right to early and mail-in voting)
purpose: Put early and mail voting into the Arizona Constitution
sponsor: Protect the Vote Arizona (funded largely by United Food and Commercial Workers and other unions, per KJZZ)
circulation_firm: unknown (Lumen Strategies managed the campaign; Lumen is a PR/consulting firm, not confirmed as the signature vendor)
evidence_note: Dropped because the expected validity rate was too low. Arizona Agenda said the drive was 'largely undertaken by volunteers' (about 1,700 circulators). It is a possible 2028 refile, but no source mentions 2028 plans.

campaign_name: Axon headquarters / apartments zoning referendum
purpose: Refer the city council's November 2024 approval of Axon's HQ campus and apartments to voters
sponsor: Taxpayers Against Awful Apartment Zoning Exemptions (TAAAZE); signature drive described as union-linked
signatures_required: unknown (city clerk certified it met the constitutional minimum)
evidence_note: Shows local referendum demand in Arizona. A state bill was moving to cancel the vote; whether it reached the November 2026 ballot was not verified.

campaign_name: NO VERIFIED ACTIVE PAID PROJECT
purpose: unknown
signatures_required: 2026-cycle reference: 383,923 constitutional / 255,949 statutory / 127,975 referendum (new thresholds are set after the Nov 2026 election)
evidence_note: Checked: AZ SOS initiative, referendum, and IRR pages (no 2028 filings shown; none for the 2026 legislative session). The recall list at apps.arizona.vote/electioninfo/IRR/69 was blocked and not read. Searched for 2028 Arizona initiative filings and found none. Firms known in the AZ market (KJZZ, 2024): Petition Partners (Andrew Chavez; about $30/hr starting, up to about $55/hr) and Advanced Micro Targeting ($29/hr reported). AZ bans per-signature pay on initiatives. Next step: read the SOS paid/out-of-state circulator registry and the apps.arizona.vote IRR list directly.

campaign_name: Protect Kids Colorado Initiatives #108, #109, #110 (now Propositions 133, 134, 135)
purpose: #108 life sentence for child sex trafficking; #109 restrict transgender students in sports; #110 ban certain gender-affirming procedures for minors
sponsor: Protect Kids Colorado (Executive Director Erin Lee; founder Kevin Lundberg); Protect our Children Issue Committee for fundraising
circulation_firm: Taylor Petition Management (Tracy Taylor), registered with the state for #108-110
deadline: #108 Feb 16, 2026; #109 and #110 Feb 20, 2026 (all submitted by Feb 20)
signatures_collected: Group said more than 170,000 submitted for each
evidence_note: Confirmed paid by the end: the drive switched from volunteers to a licensed paid petition entity (Taylor Petition Management), and all three qualified as Props 133-135. Proves Taylor Petition Management is active in Colorado.

campaign_name: Initiative 177 - right to buy and use natural gas for cooking and heating
purpose: Constitutional right to purchase and sell natural gas for homes and businesses
sponsor: Advance Colorado; funders for signatures Colorado Dawn and A Common Sense America
deadline: Filed June 24, 2026; verification due by Aug 21, 2026
budget_or_spend: Colorado Dawn $750,000 for signatures; A Common Sense America $625,000 to help collect signatures (per KUNC)
evidence_note: About $1.375M was earmarked for signatures, which is strong evidence of paid circulation. Advance Colorado is linked to 6 of the 13 citizen initiatives on the 2026 CO ballot (Amendments 81, 82, 85, 86 and Props 132, 136), making it the largest repeat buyer of petition work in the region. KUNC puts the cost at $1M-$3M per measure. Firm names are in the CO SOS paid-circulator reports and TRACER, which were not read.

campaign_name: Killin for Colorado - candidate ballot-access petition
purpose: Collect signatures to put a Democratic candidate on the 2026 ballot
deadline: unknown (2026 candidate petition period is over)
evidence_note: The job posting confirms a paid circulator role, but it is undated and tied to the 2026 ballot, so it has expired. It shows 503 Strategies does paid candidate petitioning in Colorado.

campaign_name: Landslide Political - candidate signature gathering and canvassing (Colorado)
purpose: Signature gathering to qualify 2026 candidates for the Colorado ballot, plus door-to-door canvassing
contact: Apply via the Recruitee posting; no phone or email listed
evidence_note: The posting is still live but undated and refers to 2026 ballot qualification, which is over. Landslide keeps standing postings, so it could re-staff for 2027 municipal or 2028 work. That is unconfirmed.

campaign_name: Denver force-feeding / foie gras ban initiated ordinance
purpose: Ban force-feeding birds and the sale of force-fed products in Denver
evidence_note: The only citizen-initiated Denver measure for Nov 2026 per Brownstein. Whether circulators were paid or volunteers is unknown.

campaign_name: 2027 municipal elections - candidate nominating petitions (Colorado Springs Apr 6, 2027; Denver 2027 municipal)
purpose: Candidate petitions for Colorado Springs Mayor and 3 At-Large Council seats, plus district seats; Denver 2027 municipal candidate petitions of nomination
deadline: Colorado Springs candidate filing Jan 4-25, 2027; Denver deadline per the 2027 candidate packet (not read in detail)
contact: Colorado Springs City Clerk; Denver Clerk and Recorder Elections Division
evidence_note: This is a real upcoming petition window. Paid circulation is NOT confirmed; municipal candidate petitions are often volunteer-gathered. Also, Colorado's 2027-28 statewide title board list could not be read (the SOS 2027-2028 filings page was blocked), so statewide 2028 filings are unverified. Any paid entity must be licensed by the CO SOS and its circulators must wear 'PAID CIRCULATOR' badges.

campaign_name: Repeal of Independent Redistricting Commission and Standards Act (direct initiative)
purpose: Repeal Prop 4 (2018) anti-gerrymandering law and undo the court-imposed congressional map
sponsor: Utahns for Representative Government (GOP-aligned; announced by Utah GOP chair Robert Axson)
signatures_required: About 141,000 (8% of active voters) plus thresholds in 26 of 29 Senate districts
deadline: Packets due Feb 15, 2026; final determination: Insufficient
evidence_note: A 200K-signature drive in about 4 months suggests paid circulation, but no firm or payment was found. Lt. Governor's list shows it insufficient.

campaign_name: H.B. 267 Public Sector Labor Union Amendments Referendum
purpose: Repeal the 2025 ban on public-sector collective bargaining
deadline: Filed 03.08.2025; qualified, but the Legislature then repealed the bill, so it is off the 2026 ballot
evidence_note: This 2025 drive is finished. It shows Utah unions can field a large referendum within about 30 days. Paid share unknown.

campaign_name: AX THE TAX - Salt Lake County property tax referendum
purpose: Overturn the 14.65% county property-tax increase in the 2026 budget
sponsor: AX THE TAX residents' group led by Goud Maragani (with Phil Lyman helping)
evidence_note: This volunteer-style drive failed badly. That is useful as a pitch case: a county referendum with a 45-day window likely needs paid field operations.

campaign_name: Landslide Political - candidate signature gathering and canvassing (Utah)
purpose: Collect signatures to put 2026 candidates on the ballot, plus canvassing
contact: Apply via the Recruitee posting; no phone or email listed
evidence_note: The postings are undated and refer to the 2026 cycle, so they are treated as expired. They confirm Landslide pays $25/hr in Utah for signature work.

campaign_name: NO VERIFIED ACTIVE PAID PROJECT
purpose: unknown
signatures_required: unknown (thresholds reset after the Nov 2026 election)
evidence_note: The Lt. Governor's list shows no currently circulating statewide initiative or referendum. All 2025 filings are insufficient, inactive, withdrawn, or moot. The next likely window is referenda on 2027 legislative session bills (filed shortly after the session ends).

campaign_name: Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act (end Idaho's abortion ban)
purpose: Restore abortion access via statute
sponsor: Idahoans United for Women and Families (Exec. Dir. Melanie Folwell)
signatures_required: 70,725 valid statewide (6%) plus 6% in 18 of 35 legislative districts
evidence_note: Whether circulators were paid is not stated in the sources. The drive is completed.

campaign_name: Idaho medical cannabis initiative
purpose: Legalize medical cannabis
circulation_firm: Two unnamed paid vendors (the original vendor's work is under scrutiny; a second firm was brought in late)
signatures_collected: Max 58,024 certified; threshold met in only 13 districts
evidence_note: Paid circulation is confirmed, but the drive failed. The sponsor is weighing legal remedies. A vendor-quality failure like this is a pitch angle for a 2028 retry. Vendor names are unknown.

campaign_name: NO VERIFIED ACTIVE PAID PROJECT
purpose: unknown
evidence_note: Searched for Idaho 2028 initiative filings and current recalls and found no verified circulating petition. Boise recall results were historical. The voteidaho.gov active-initiative list was not read.

campaign_name: Initiative 194 - prohibit entity political spending
purpose: Bar corporations, nonprofits, and trade associations from contributing to candidate and ballot-measure elections
deadline: June 19, 2026 to counties; July 17, 2026 to SOS
budget_or_spend: unknown (Ballotpedia: 2024 MT qualified initiatives averaged about $1.7M and about $27.42 per required signature)
evidence_note: Paid share unknown. 12 initiatives were filed for 2026 in Montana; only I-194, CI-132, and CI-133 submitted signatures.

campaign_name: CI-133 - initiative and referendum rights in the Declaration of Rights
purpose: Guarantee impartial, predictable, transparent initiative processes
deadline: June 19, 2026 to counties; July 17, 2026 to SOS
evidence_note: Paid share unknown. CI-132 (nonpartisan judicial elections; sponsor not found) also submitted signatures for 2026.

campaign_name: NO VERIFIED ACTIVE PAID PROJECT
purpose: unknown
evidence_note: Montana statewide gathering for 2026 could not start before June 19, 2025, so 2028 gathering likely cannot start until mid-2027 (inferred; not verified). No 2028 filings were found. The SOS proposed-ballot-issues page was not read.

campaign_name: People's Initiative to Limit Property Tax through a Homeowner's Property Exemption
purpose: Homeowner property-tax exemption / limits
deadline: Certified for the 2026 General Election ballot
evidence_note: The only Wyoming initiative listed by the SOS. Paid or volunteer status is unknown.

campaign_name: NO VERIFIED ACTIVE PAID PROJECT
purpose: unknown
evidence_note: The SOS page lists no current referenda and no other initiatives in circulation. Referenda must be filed within 90 days after a session adjourns.

campaign_name: New Mexico Forward Party - minor-party candidate ballot access (Perls for U.S. Senate; Vigil for State Auditor)
purpose: Put Forward Party candidates on the 2026 ballot
sponsor: New Mexico Forward Party (chair Bob Perls)
deadline: Passed; lawsuit lost at district court and 10th Circuit (Sept 2026); SCOTUS emergency request filed Sept 15, 2026
signatures_collected: unknown (fell short of 14,000; party says it exceeded major-party thresholds)
evidence_note: This shows unmet demand for minor-party ballot access work in New Mexico (a 14K+ signature bar). Whether any circulators were paid is unknown.

campaign_name: NO VERIFIED ACTIVE PAID PROJECT
purpose: unknown
evidence_note: New Mexico has no citizen initiative process, only a high-bar referendum (a 2019 attempt was found; no current one). Searches for 2026 recall and municipal referendum petitions (Albuquerque, Santa Fe, Las Cruces) found nothing current. The next likely work is 2027 local candidate petitions and 2028 minor-party/independent ballot access.
